explain.say: The common cuckoo never builds a nest or raises its young. It lays its eggs in other birds' nests, such as reed warblers', and the hosts raise the cuckoo chick as their own. This is called brood parasitism.

explain.say: The female watches a host nest, then swoops in while the owners are away, removes one egg and lays her own in about ten seconds. Each female specialises on one host species, and her eggs often match theirs.

explain.say: The lone cuckoo chick begs so fast that it sounds like a whole brood, so its foster parents keep feeding it even when it is far bigger than they are. Hosts and cuckoos are locked in an arms race of tricks and defences.

left.title: Host defences
points: Spot and throw out odd eggs

faq.q: How does a cuckoo egg fool the host?
faq.a: Each female cuckoo lays eggs that closely match the colour and pattern of her chosen host's eggs, and she lays very quickly while the hosts are away. Hosts that spot an odd egg may throw it out, so better copies survive.
asks: Why do cuckoo eggs look like other eggs?
How do cuckoos lay eggs in other nests?

faq.q: Why does a cuckoo chick push out the other eggs?
faq.a: With no rivals, the cuckoo chick gets all the food the foster parents bring. It has a hollow in its back that helps it balance eggs and push them over the edge, an instinct it shows within hours of hatching.
asks: Why do cuckoo chicks kill the other chicks?
How does a baby cuckoo throw out eggs?

faq.q: Why do host birds keep feeding a giant chick?
faq.a: Parent birds feed whatever begs in their nest, and the cuckoo chick's rapid calls sound like a whole brood of hungry chicks. Its wide orange gape also triggers feeding.
asks: Why don't warblers notice the cuckoo chick?
Why do small birds feed big cuckoos?

faq.q: How does a young cuckoo know it is a cuckoo?
faq.a: By instinct. It is raised by another species, yet it makes cuckoo calls and later migrates alone to Africa, finding its way without ever being shown.
asks: How do cuckoos learn to be cuckoos?

faq.q: Do other birds lay eggs in other nests?
faq.a: Yes. Cowbirds in the Americas, honeyguides in Africa and some ducks are also brood parasites, and many hosts have evolved defences against them.
asks: Which birds lay eggs in other birds' nests?

facts: A female common cuckoo can lay an egg in a host nest in about ten seconds.
A single cuckoo chick's begging call sounds like a whole brood of reed warbler chicks (Davies and colleagues, 1998).
